chunk_map.heading: Phase 1: Read what the failed run did
Keep Claude honest, make it dig
Phase 2: Match each failure to the check that catches it
Phase 3: Build the verifier for your worst failure
Phase 4: Write the reference and plan.md
Check both files are for the agent, not you
Send it off and read the report cold

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: a reader loses the thread when a pronoun/noun has no antecedent they can hold. Checked every chunk. 'the failed run' / 'the un-packaged run' / 'the m4/<slug> branch' (chunks 0-1) resolve via the session-artifact carve-out (student's own M4 work). 'each named failure' (chunk 3, line 70) resolves against the three lenses named in Phase 1's fenced prompt (lines 51-53), which the sequential reader has already passed. 'you will meet the word again' (chunk 4, line 101) is a forward-looking aside, not a referent requiring resolution now. Chunk 6's 'Reference'/'plan.md' are defined in the same chunk they're bolded in. No unresolved referent found; harm absent.

Harm: a callback that depends on which file/module sits where breaks under re-sequencing. Chunk 2 line 64: 'Same prior as the repo read in Module 1: assume about 10% of the account misrepresents the run...' names the source (Module 1) AND unpacks the claim in the same sentence, satisfying the carve-out's bar. Chunk 10 line 200: 'the field has a name for this move ... see [What packaging is](lectures/what-packaging-is.md)' names the document in the link text (sentence still reads with the link stripped). Chunk 11 line 236: 'Same cancel-is-legit rule as the un-packaged session: stopping when the trace is enough is the result' unpacks the rule inline. No position-dependent phrasing ('the opening lecture', 'the previous module') found. Harm absent.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Every backward reference points at a beat that exists.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: a backward/forward beat-reference that names a beat the current module set doesn't have strands the reader. Chunk 11 (line 234, module-flag branch): 'The walk-away report at the close is what Module 6 opens on.' Verified against site/layouts/curriculum.js MODULES array: this file's host module is 'learn-from-the-test' (M5), and the very next module is 'spot-gaps-build-the-loop' (M6) -- matching the flag condition exactly. The referenced beat exists. Harm absent.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Live-demo beats survive a text read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: a guess-before-reveal instruction whose answer is narrated above it, so the beat is already spoiled on a text read. No guess/predict-then-reveal construction appears anywhere in this file's body -- the file is a diagnose-then-build-then-resend exercise, not a live-demo prediction beat. Rule doesn't apply; no harm to check for.

Harm: a chunk that says nothing on its own projects as a blank beat. Shortest chunk is 9 ('Approve', lines 182-185): 'Say *lock it in.* The agent writes both files.' -- terse but self-carrying (names the trigger phrase and its effect), not a wait-state bullet like the compendium's canonical orphan example. Harm absent across all 13 chunks.

Harm: a header the chunk's own content contradicts misleads a reader who only skims headers. Every header (Phase 1-5, 'Keep Claude honest, make it dig', 'Approve', etc.) matches its chunk's content on inspection. Harm absent.

Harm: repo-authored prose tics (triadic constructions, self-grading, hedged numbers, abstraction stacks, empty-leg verb triplets) read as filler on a wall-projected slide. Grepped body for 'Not X. Not Y.' constructions, anaphora triples, superlatives, abstraction-noun stacks: none found. The one number+hedge instance ('about 10%', chunk 2 line 64) carries an explicit maintainer accept-note ('M1's double-hedge stays M1's, so check_slides.md's number-plus-retraction sub-item does not fire here') naming exactly this passage -- checked per the maintainer-accept-note gate before flagging. Harm absent.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Internal dialect never lands on a slide.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: repo/maintainer vocabulary (surface-as-noun, compendium, forcing function, beat, mood) smuggled onto a slide reads as jargon to an engineer in the room. Grepped body for these terms: no hits. 'HOX', 'Session', canonical widget names are architecture-mandated chrome, not dialect. 'stop-hook' (chunk 4) is Claude Code product terminology, cited to the cc-hooks-docs source in backing, not repo-internal jargon. Harm absent.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Emphasis budget -- bold is for handles, and go very lightly.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: bold-monoculture (whole sentences/leads bolded) buries the actual handles and reads as noise on a slide. Bold in body is confined to title-page/widget-chrome labels (chunk 0), the Phase 3 verifier-shape handles (chunk 4, one per bullet), the Phase 4 stop-gate handle (chunk 7 blockquote), and two coined-term handles 'Reference'/'plan.md' introduced on their own definitional chunk (chunk 6, one handle per bullet, consistent with the 'one handle per law/consolidation slide' allowance). No whole-sentence bold, no bullet-opens-with-bold monoculture. Note for the maintainer, not a rule violation: the file's own Emphasis paragraph (line 153) lists title-page/widget-chrome/Phase-3-menu/Phase-4-stop-gate as the full bold inventory and doesn't mention chunk 6's two handles -- the note appears to have gone stale relative to the current body, worth a one-line update, but the rendered bold itself stays within budget so no REVISE.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Presence precedes content -- verify against the composed deck, not long-read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: content invisible in the default Slides deck (phase-less sections dropped by buildDeckModel) gets audited as if present. All content sits under the exercise's normal ## structure inside the exercise file, which is included via the module's phase--exercise wrapper -- no phase-less prose section here. Harm absent.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Numbering -- position is computed, content ordinals are linted.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: hand-numbered or inconsistent Phase/Step ordinals strand in-file cross-references. Phase headers run 1,2,3,4,5 consecutively; in-file forward refs ('Phase 3 builds the verifier...Phase 4 assembles...', chunk 3; 'Fire it once before Phase 4', chunk 5) all resolve to real later headers. Confirmed mechanically: node scripts/check-slide-numbering.js reports 'OK -- 61 files, Phase/Step numbering consistent' (this file included in the scanned set). Harm absent.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Page geometry dies at the cut; reading order survives.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: a positional pointer ('below', 'above') aims at a wall once the renderer cuts at ##. Chunk 11 line 212: 'the re-send prompt below stands alone' -- the referenced prompt (lines 218-232) sits in the SAME chunk, matching the compendium's canonical same-chunk-passes example exactly. No other below/above/further-down phrasing found. Confirmed mechanically: node scripts/check-slide-deixis.js reports 'OK -- 61 files, no page-geometry pointers across the slide cut.' Harm absent.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: In-deck links work now; whether they EARN their place is open.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: a dead in-deck link (mechanism) or an unnamed, geometry-located link (open question, now settled as no-rule). One link in body: chunk 10 line 200, '[What packaging is](lectures/what-packaging-is.md)' -- names the document in the link text, mechanism fixed 2026-08-12 per the compendium's own note, no rule to apply beyond naming. Harm absent.
